newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gov rejects church mediation with guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gov rejects church mediation with guerrillas.

text.p: An offer by the Roman Catholic Church to mediate proposed peace talks with the leftist Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) was rejected on Thursday by the governor of Oaxaca state.
A bishop the Mexican state had offered on Wednesday to serve as a mediator between the guerrillas and the government.
"We don't need mediators for anything, much less the church. God help us!" Oaxaca Governor Diodoro Carrasco Altamirano said during a working trip to the small rural town of Ixtlan de Juarez.
The EPR first appeared in the southwestern state of Guerrero in June and has attacked military targets in several states, including Oaxaca, which is just south of Guerrero.
Their most serious operation came on August 28-29, attacking several states at the same time, including one military target in the state of Mexico adjoining Mexico City.
The government said 15 were killed and 22 wounded in those attacks, but EPR activity has been minimal since then.
The Mexican government has refused to negotiate, calling the EPR "terrorist."
Carrasco, the Oaxaca governor, said his state would be willing to talk "if somebody would show his face, publicly identify himself and propose a negotiation."
EPR cadres always appear masked in public.

The bishop of Tehuantepec, Arturo Lona Reyes, proposed that the Catholic Church serve as a mediator between the armed group and the government in the same way the church has in southeastern Chiapas state with the unrelated Zapatista rebels.
The church "would give more confidence to the people in this negotiation," Lona said. "I just hope it happens."
The EPR has ruled out negotiations, saying it aims to rewrite the constitution, transform the economy and create a "Popular Democratic Republic."
